links.outcome: Baseline readability grade level of institutional consent forms versus recommended sixth grade
links.effect: Original forms averaged 14.1 ± 1.3 grade levels, far above the recommended sixth-grade level.

links.outcome: Readability of LLM-rewritten consent forms versus originals
links.effect: First LLM revision improved readability to an 8.8 ± 1.2 grade level (P < 0.01), a five-grade reduction; second revision showed no further improvement (9.9 ± 1.2; P = 0.87).
links.quote: First LLM revision significantly improved readability to an 8.8 ± 1.2 grade level (P < 0.01), a five-grade reduction.

links.outcome: Fidelity of LLM-simplified text: precision, recall, hallucinations and omissions
links.effect: Mean F1 0.71 ± 0.26, precision 0.95 ± 0.06, recall 0.62 ± 0.16: few hallucinations but frequent omissions.
links.quote: The mean F1 score was 0.71 ± 0.26, with high precision (0.95 ± 0.06) but lower recall (0.62 ± 0.16), indicating few hallucinations but frequent content omissions.

links.outcome: Content omissions in LLM-edited consent forms requiring human review
links.effect: LLM editing caused substantial content omissions; greater reading-level reductions associated with decreased fidelity (r = 0.73, P < 0.01).
links.quote: LLM-based editing significantly improved consent form readability but resulted in substantial content omissions.
